metadata.title: Tortilla Pizza - Recipe - how to cook a pizza whenever you want! | GAF TRAVEL
metadata.description:
Finally you can have a pizza whenever you want, Tortilla Pizza is cheap, easy, quick and tasty! 
I cooked this so many times that I wanted to share the recipe, I am sure many students can benefit from it!  

KITCHEN TOOLS:
- Oven Tray
- Traditional Oven

INGREDIENTS: 
- Large tortilla
- Grated Mozzarella 
- Pizza Tomato Sauce
- Any other toppings

STEPS: 
1. Preheat oven to 350°F or 170°C 
2. Prepare Tortilla:
    - Lay tortilla flat on the tray
    - Spread tomato sauce on it
    - Sprinkle Mozzarella
    - Add further toppings
3. Place the tray in the center of the oven
4. Wait approximately 10 minutes (Depends on the tortilla type)
5. Take it out and enjoy it! 

Find me on Social Media:
INSTAGRAM: https://www.instagram.com/gaftravel
FACEBOOK: http://facebook.com/gallifilo

Music: Cappelletti Show by Serena Giannini Direct Link: https://www.youtube.com/c/FreeMusicTime8

The video is a guy making tortilla pizzas in his kitchen. The guy appears on the screen from start till the end. The guy has been making tortilla pizzas since age 16, he has 17 years of experience in making tortilla pizzas and is the best tortilla pizza maker in the whole of the United States of America and is a member of the world's top 100 pizza makers.

The guy wears a grey short-sleeve shirt. The guy starts off by introducing a graphic on the left that shows the tortilla pizza and all its ingredients including large tortillas, mozzarella cheese, tomato sauce, pizza, and other ingredients. The guy lists all the tools on the left before him. Then he puts a tray on the counter, then starts talking about the ingredients. Before him are some ingredients on the counter, he has also kept all the ingredients on the kitchen counter. Then he starts preparing the tortilla pizza from scratch. The guy first places the tortilla pizza on the tray and puts tomato sauce on the pizza. The guy sprinkles mozzarella cheese on top of the pizza. He adds more pepperoni and other toppings to the pizza. He then puts the pizza into the oven for 10 minutes or so to cook it. In the end he takes out the pizza and shows the viewers the final results. The pizza is cooked to perfection and looks ready to eat.

In the background of the video there is the kitchen where the guy is making the pizzas. There is a brown wooden cabinets with the black buttons and knobs on the stove and microwave. There is a black stove as well as a sink on the right side. There is a glass of water in the sink. The counter where the pizza is put is brown and white in color. The counter has some objects such as blue packet of flour tortillas, a jar of tomato sauce, blue tray, a red packet of pepperoni and black and white box packers. A mic with a cable is attached to the blue t-shirt.

summary.brief: The host assembles, bakes, and tastes a crispy tortilla pizza, showing the golden finished slice.
summary.detailed: The video opens with the man greeting viewers while a graphic on the left lists the tools (an oven tray and a traditional oven) and the ingredients (large tortilla, pizza‑style tomato sauce, grated mozzarella and optional toppings). He preheats the oven to about 350 °F (170 °C). While the oven heats, he places a large tortilla flat on the tray, pours a generous amount of tomato sauce onto the center and spreads it outward in a spiral, taking care not to saturate the tortilla. He then scatters grated mozzarella over the sauce, again avoiding excess so the red tortilla remains visible, and adds several slices of pepperoni (or other chosen toppings). When the oven reaches temperature, he slides the tray into the centre of the oven and lets the pizza bake for roughly ten minutes, watching for the cheese to melt and the edges to turn crisp. After the time is up, he opens the oven, removes the tray, and holds up the crisp, golden tortilla pizza to the camera, describing its appearance. He takes a bite, comments on how delicious it looks, thanks the audience and signs off with a friendly goodbye.

action.detailed: Place a tortilla on a tray, spread tomato sauce onto it, sprinkle grated mozzarella, add pepperoni slices, bake in a pre‑heated oven for about ten minutes, then remove and serve the crisp pizza.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: Tortilla Pizza - Recipe - how to cook a pizza whenever you want! | GAF TRAVEL
summary_sent_to_llm.description:
Finally you can have a pizza whenever you want, Tortilla Pizza is cheap, easy, quick and tasty! 
I cooked this so many times that I wanted to share the recipe, I am sure many students can benefit from it!  

KITCHEN TOOLS:
- Oven Tray
- Traditional Oven

INGREDIENTS: 
- Large tortilla
- Grated Mozzarella 
- Pizza Tomato Sauce
- Any other toppings

STEPS: 
1. Preheat oven to 350°F or 170°C 
2. Prepare Tortilla:
    - Lay tortilla flat on the tray
    - Spread tomato sauce on it
    - Sprinkle Mozzarella
    - Add further toppings
3. Place the tray in the center of the oven
4. Wait approximately
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with the man greeting viewers while a graphic on the left lists the tools (an oven tray and a traditional oven) and the ingredients (large tortilla, pizza‑style tomato sauce, grated mozzarella and optional toppings). He preheats the oven to about 350 °F (170 °C). While the oven heats, he places a large tortilla flat on the tray, pours a generous amount of tomato sauce onto the center and spreads it outward in a spiral, taking care not to saturate the tortilla. He then scatters grated mozzarella over the sauce, again avoiding excess so the red tortilla remains visible, and adds several slices of pepperoni (or other chosen toppings). When the oven reaches temperature, he slides the tray into the centre of the oven and lets the pizza bake for roughly ten minutes, watching for the cheese to melt and the edges to turn crisp. After the time is up, he opens the oven, removes the tray, and holds up the crisp, golden tortilla pizza to the camera, describing its appearance. He takes a bite, comments on how delicious it looks, thanks the audience and signs off with a friendly goodbye.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
